absent: Allocation and lifetime of per-node processor sets and early node resolver implementation.
Address lookup, huge-page detection and page attribute mutation primitives.
Interval reservation, release, allowance policy and kernel map synchronization.
Platform untracked-range predicate and RAM range walk driver.
Cache mode to protection conversion tables and full hardware register encoding.
Concurrency and ordering guarantees for background self-test execution.
Verbose flag control interface and large-page size selection across builds.

findings.text: Expose membership management binding a processor to the processor set of its node as determined by early firmware identification. Insertion makes that processor present in the corresponding set, removal makes it absent, and both preserve all other entries. Two build flavours provide the same contract, one acting directly and one delegating through a diagnostic path that first resolves the node.

Provide query from processor number to node number using per-processor storage. When only early boot storage is available the query still answers from there while signalling misuse for diagnostic purposes. Once normal per-processor storage is established the query answers from it without diagnostic side effects.

Diagnostic variant of membership update requires a valid node and an allocated per-node set; an invalid node causes silent return after relying on resolver diagnostics, while a missing set causes error reporting with trace and no mutation. On valid inputs it either inserts or removes the given processor according to a Boolean flag and then emits a debug record describing the resulting set.

Emulation remap rewrites the firmware identifier to node table from physical identifiers to emulated identifiers by reverse lookup in a caller supplied translation array, leaving sentinel entries untouched and substituting zero when no translation matches. A companion boot query reports the end of the low direct memory area as the physical address derived from the maximum low frame number.

Test census record holds tallies for small mappings and for two larger mapping granularities plus a count of executable mappings, together with observed minimum and maximum executable addresses. All fields use signed machine word storage and are reset before each census pass.

Census over the directly mapped physical range classifies each resident entry by mapping granularity and executability, advancing by the covered extent for large entries and by one page otherwise, skipping unmapped entries as misses. It enforces that present large entries carry the large-page marker, records executable span, optionally logs a summary, and finally requires that accounted pages plus misses exactly cover the walked range.

Self-test marker is a page protection value carrying a software-reserved bit, with a predicate that reports whether a given entry carries that bit. Presence of the marker indicates a region currently under test modification.

Self-test progresses through snapshot, randomized mutation, verification, restoration and final verification. Mutation selects non-overlapping present runs of uniform protection tracked by a bitmap, applies the marker through three rotating interfaces, and demands small granularity without huge status plus marker presence. Restoration clears the marker through one interface and demands absence. Any lookup, status or level mismatch accumulates failure leading to warning and error return, otherwise success.
Offer page-frame array interface for setting a caller protection mask over a counted list, delegating to a generic set-clear primitive in array mode with an empty clear mask and non-atomic behaviour.

Background execution entry repeatedly invokes the self-test at thirty second interruptible intervals until stop is requested or a run fails, reducing verbosity after each successful run. A starter entry creates the named worker thread and wakes it, warning if creation fails, and always reports successful initiation.

Global PAT control consists of a read-mostly disabled flag whose initial value is the negation of the build-time PAT option, a write-once-after-init storage for the PAT hardware register value, and an empty log prefix wrapper. The flag gates all higher PAT behaviour.

Disable operation is idempotent: if already disabled it does nothing, otherwise it marks disabled, logs the supplied reason under the PAT subsystem tag, and removes PAT capability from the caching control mask. A boot option entry unconditionally invokes this operation with a fixed administrative reason.
Debug control is a mutable integer defaulting to off, enabled by a boot option entry that sets it on. It has no other side effects in the observed fragments.

Page metadata encoding uses two architecture-reserved flag positions to represent four memory types, with writeback as zero, write-combining using the lower flag, uncached-minus using the upper flag, and writethrough using both, plus combined mask and inverted clear mask constants derived from the same positions.

Translation from three-bit hardware PAT value to architectural cache mode maps the six defined encodings to their matching modes and folds any other value to writeback, while writing a four-character textual label for the selected mode into caller memory. A helper macro constructs mode enumerators from type tokens.

Boot initialization selects a PAT table according to capability and platform: missing CPU support or empty firmware value disables PAT and installs a compatible table; virtualized firmware keeps the firmware value without programming hardware; affected legacy processor families install an errata-limited table using only low slots; otherwise a full table with writeback, combining, uncached variants and writethrough plus writeprotect is installed and capability is advertised. Cache mode table is then built from high to low slot with a combined log line. Secondary processor entry requires PAT support when boot enabled it, otherwise it aborts, and on success programs the saved register value followed by a global flush.

All interval-tree reservation, lookup and enumeration accesses are serialized by a single spinlock dedicated to memory type state. The lock is held only around tree query or copy operations and released before returning to callers.
Range classification record contains current frame number cursor plus two integer flags recording whether any RAM and any non-RAM has been observed. Cursor advances monotonically during walks.

Walk callback merges gap detection and presence into the classification record, updates the cursor to the end of the visited extent, and signals termination only after both RAM and non-RAM have been observed.

Single-page type resolution prefers untracked platform ranges as writeback, then delegates RAM pages to per-page stored type, otherwise consults the interval database under lock returning the stored type on hit and uncached-minus on miss.

Interval lookup has two build variants with identical signature: a fallback that always reports absence, and a tree search over the inclusive page-sized interval beginning at the queried address. Callers treat absence as uncached-minus outside RAM paths.

Provide predicate reporting immunity to uncached MTRR effects when the resolved type is uncached, uncached-minus or write-combining. Provide paired reservation interfaces that reserve an I/O byte range as write-combining and release it, translating size to an end address.

Direct physical access protection either preserves or strips encryption based on range encryption status. An authorization helper grants unconditionally when PAT is off, denies forbidden ranges, otherwise selects uncached-minus for synchronized opens and writeback otherwise, installing the choice by replacing only cache bits via a conversion helper.

Reservation distinguishes RAM from I/O. RAM paths require PAT enabled to enforce type agreement with the first page, warning and coercing caller protection on mismatch but never refcounting. I/O paths delegate to the interval reserve primitive, validate coerced types against allowance policy with cleanup and error on violation, coerce caller protection when allowed, and synchronize the kernel map with cleanup on sync failure.

Frame-map tracking forwards establishment and release to the reservation primitives using shifted physical addresses, with release acting only on non-RAM ranges. A setup helper requires PAT enabled and uniform resolved type across every page in the range, installing that type into caller protection or failing without mutation on heterogeneity.
Provide pure protection transformers returning a copy with cache mode forced to write-combining or writethrough respectively, leaving other bits unchanged.

Indexed enumeration allocates a fresh record, copies the one-based nth interval under lock, and returns null on allocation failure or out-of-range position with cleanup. The fallback copy primitive always reports success without mutation, while the tree variant walks from zero to maximum counting entries and copies on exact match. A sequential debug interface prints a header at start, iterates by incrementing position with per-step release, formats each entry as address bounds plus type name, and registers a read-only debug file only when PAT is active.

Memory type interval record stores inclusive start, exclusive end, cached subtree maximum end, cache mode, and intrusive tree linkage. Helper accessors expose inclusive bounds by returning start unchanged and end decremented by one. The global cached tree root begins empty.

Misuse and failure paths include early per-processor access emitting warning with trace, missing per-node set emitting error with trace, secondary processor without PAT support aborting boot, self-test mismatches emitting error logs culminating in warning, worker creation failure triggering warning, and reservation conflicts or kernel map sync failures releasing state and returning errors.

Boot processor PAT setup and secondary processor PAT programming serve as initialization entries invoked during CPU bring-up, alongside debug list registration during late init. They establish global PAT state before any reservation or mapping activity.

Three PAT register configurations are defined as facts: firmware-disabled emulation mapping slots to writeback, writethrough, uncached-minus and uncached repeating; errata-limited mapping low slots to writeback, combining, uncached-minus and uncached repeating; full support mapping slots zero through seven to writeback, combining, uncached-minus, uncached, writeback reserved, writeprotect, uncached-minus reserved and writethrough. Slot seven uses writethrough to fail safe toward uncached on ignored high bit.
Memory type private header defines a once-only inclusion guard macro preventing repeated processing.
Self-test sizing uses three hundred address-length trials over one hundred auxiliary pages, with large granularities of two megabytes on common builds and one gigabyte on wide builds.
